<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0967cbe6a2919413952ab3521b9d7771a5398274`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0967cbe6a2919413952ab3521b9d7771a5398274` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `902129291a68188acc2c9f4d8051c6eeeb34d678` — the merge of head `3025ade8eb1310b51a3aec79d03d824b56f944e4` into base `0967cbe6a2919413952ab3521b9d7771a5398274`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 902129291a68188acc2c9f4d8051c6eeeb34d678 && git checkout 902129291a68188acc2c9f4d8051c6eeeb34d678
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0967cbe6a2919413952ab3521b9d7771a5398274 3025ade8eb1310b51a3aec79d03d824b56f944e4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0967cbe6a2919413952ab3521b9d7771a5398274 && git merge --no-ff 3025ade8eb1310b51a3aec79d03d824b56f944e4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0967cbe6a2919413952ab3521b9d7771a5398274
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0967cbe6a2919413952ab3521b9d7771a5398274` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：保存一份示例数据时，如果它要灌进的对象根本不存在（比如名字少写了前缀），会直接报错，并告诉你改成正确的对象名或先建对象。发布后的检查也会说“对象不存在”，不再让人“再发布一次”。
- 为什么做：以前这种示例数据能存进去，发布也显示成功，但其实一条记录都没加载；提示还让人反复重新发布，怎么试都没用。
- 出错会怎样：只会多拦下这一种必然加载不了的保存。已经存下的旧示例数据照样能发布和恢复，对象只是草稿时草稿示例数据仍可保存。
- 要你做什么：不需要你做任何事。它收紧了一条保存规则，席位会安排一次约定审核，然后由区域落地。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#5 · head `468886742c089180014c6d8dc1da1d0c68b59405` · 2026-11-19T08:24Z

- **形态** — 12 files, +387/−48:
  - `metadata-protocol` source: `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts`, `protocol-save.ts`, `protocol.ts`, `build-probes.ts`, `build-probes.user-text.ts`
  - tests, including three objectql fixtures
  - one ADR-0087 semantic ledger entry under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/`
  - one changeset

  `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35388`: not governed, under the 3000-line limit. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `minor`. The level is right for the kind. The ADR-0087 marker reads `registered seed-object-unknown-refused` and matches the new entry.
- **Fixes vs card #34864**
  - **Who asks.** `seedExternalIdSaveRefusal` gains `door?: 'save'`. Only `saveMetaItem` passes it, and only when the write is not `migrate-stored`. The publish promotion and the restore doors pass nothing, so a seed stored before this rule still publishes, and its load reports the missing object (#27393).
  - **What counts as resolved.** A same-batch draft object, or a registered object; a dependency package's object is served by the same registry read. On a draft save, an object that is itself only a draft is deferred to publish, as before. The existence check now runs before the keyed-mode check, so a non-keyed (`insert`) seed is judged for its object too.
  - **"Unknown" follows the #28990 grant rule** (`unknownSeedObjectRefusal`):
    - a registry with no `getObject` cannot say a name is unknown, so nothing is refused;
    - a stored or code-defined object that `readMetaItem` returns is known;
    - a `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (a name two packages hold) counts as known;
    - any other read error propagates.
  - **The answer.** `422 INVALID_METADATA`, one finding at `object` naming the seed, the object and the fix. The fix wording differs for a draft save and a publish save.
  - **The probe.** `seed_not_applied` adds cause `missing` only when both hold: the engine's `getSchema` answers no object, and no published object of that name is held. Anything else stays `unreadable` ("publish again"). The `message` and `fix` name the object, and `userMessage` carries the `missing` arm in the platform locales.
- **Points weighed**
  - The draft deferral, publish promotion, restore doors and `migrate-stored` re-saves are unchanged. Each is pinned as a control.
  - The old control "an object neither registered nor drafted is not judged here" is replaced by the refusal, which is the card's ask. Accepted.
  - The three objectql fixtures and two publish-receipt tests used a seed on a missing object to stand for a stored row. They now write it through the platform's `migrate-stored` re-save, which is the honest spelling of "stored before the rule". Accepted.
  - `protocol.ts` sits at its facade ceiling, so its docblock is shortened and points at `unknownSeedObjectRefusal`'s docblock. Accepted.
  - The cancelled-by-push Type Check on `913a0d5dc` contained 0 `error TS`. It is not attributed to this PR, and this head is green.
- **Changeset** — read sentence by sentence against the diff. These all match:
  - every caller of the door;
  - the 422 at `object`, and the old 200-then-empty-load behaviour;
  - draft versus live acceptance;
  - dependency and registry objects;
  - the unchanged promotion, restore and `migrate-stored` paths;
  - the fix sentence;
  - the probe's `missing` versus `unreadable` split.
  Nit, not blocking: other narrowing changesets carry a `**BREAKING**` line. This one's narrowing is declared on the `Clause-②` line only, which the ADR-0087 gate accepts.
- **Pins**
  - `protocol.seed-external-id-refusal.test.ts`:
    - an unknown object is refused on draft and on publish saves (`it.each`);
    - a publish save whose object is only a draft is refused;
    - CONTROLs pass for: a registered object (draft and live), a same-package drafted object, a `migrate-stored` re-save, the publish promotion of a seed stored before the rule, and the restore door.
  - `build-probes-user-message.test.ts`: names the missing object to the agent with the fix, and says "missing" to the person.
  - Dogfood battery green on `913a0d5dc` (report 7003357918).
- **门禁** — 73 check-runs on this head: 60 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure.
- **范围外去向** — none found.
- **L2 owed (routing)** — a `(narrowing)` declaration plus a non-test `packages/spec/src/**` path (the ledger entry) → contract review at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER. Routed to seat 5.
- **落地条款** — not governed. Base `3819afec`; main has moved K=15 first-parent commits (≥ 15), so merge main and wait for a green re-run before queueing. `git merge-tree` against current main is clean, and main has touched none of the five source files since the base. This ACCEPT carries over to the merged head if it brings nothing beyond main. pkg-1 lands after the seat's L2 record.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `468886742c089180014c6d8dc1da1d0c68b59405`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.seed-object-unknown-refused.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.user-text.ts

PR #35388, card #34864. Read: the card and its five comments, the PR body and its four comments, the net diff against `main`, and the 73 check-runs on this head (60 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure). The test files, the three objectql fixtures and the changeset prose are the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, narrowed — right.** `saveMetaItem` now refuses `422 INVALID_METADATA` at `object` a `seed` whose object nothing resolves. Before, the body was stored 200. One authored value is refused and no other value changes.
- **Accept set, not widened — right.** Every body accepted on this head was accepted on `main`. The resolution order moved ahead of the keyed-mode filter, so an `insert` or `replace` seed is now judged for its object too; that is part of the same narrowing, not a second one.
- **Public surface, unchanged — right.** `seedExternalIdSaveRefusal` gains an optional `door` argument, but the method is `private` on the protocol class and the module function is reached through that host alone. `unknownSeedObjectRefusal` is not exported. The probe keeps its one code, `seed_not_applied`; `cause: 'missing'` is a parameter of the internal sentence catalog, not an authored or exported value.
- **Doors left as they were — right, and pinned.** The publish promotion and the restore door pass no `door`, and a `migrate-stored` re-save is not asked. A seed stored before the rule still publishes and its load reports the object.
- **Spec — data only, right.** One semantic ledger file. No Zod schema, export or generated baseline moves; `Spec property liveness` and the lint lanes are green on the head.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the correct line.** The value answers one question: does the diff widen an accept set or the public surface. It does not, per ①, so the value is `no`. The arm travels beside the value and does not replace it; the changeset gate reads `no (narrowing)` as a truthful `no` with the breaking arm. `yes (narrowing)` is the spelling for a diff that widens and narrows at once, which this one is not. The line is identical on the PR body, the changeset body and both claims.
- **`Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is right**: a value an author could write is now refused. `narrowed` beside a `(narrowing)` arm is the coherent pair the gate requires.
- **Level `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is right**: a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- **ADR-0087 disposition**: the changeset carries exactly one marker, `registered seed-object-unknown-refused`, and the id is the new entry's id. `main` holds no entry of that id. `Lint · repo & tooling gates` is green on the head. This is the single disposition the gate wants; `not-required` would be refused on a `narrowed` changeset.
- N3 (nit) — the changeset names `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` alone, while the ledger entry ships in `@objectstack/spec`. The registered-entry changesets on `main` (#34613, #34776, #34682) name both. The two packages are in one fixed group, so the version is the same either way and no gate asks for it; the spec CHANGELOG simply gets no line. Accepted deviation.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dogfood battery — a re-run is owed before landing.** The newest `os-dev-report` (7003357918) opens `dogfood_battery` with `913a0d5dc` and says the head was not re-run because it adds ledger data only. The rule has no data-only exemption: the battery runs on the final head, and the `--land` gate accepts a battery sha only when it is the head or is reached from the head over merges of the base alone. `468886742` is a one-parent commit on top of `913a0d5dc`, so `--land` refuses it ("lies after the battery's sha and is not a merge"). The argument is also not safe on its merits: the spec build generates its migration registry from this directory, and the dogfood closure builds spec. To clear it, run the full battery on the head that will land and post a report whose `dogfood_battery` opens with that sha. The seat's ACCEPT already asks for a merge of `main` first (15 commits behind); a battery on `468886742` stays valid under that merge, and a battery on the merged head is valid too. This is a landing precondition. It changes no file, so this record still covers the head.
- **Spec fence**: the dev's open question (may the PR add the ledger file under the fenced `packages/spec/**`) was answered by the amended claim 7003076381. Answered.
- **Three objectql fixtures and the replaced control test**: inside the amended claim; lane seat's ACCEPT.
- **Restore door not judged for the object**: within the card, which covers the save door and the remedy text only. See N2.
- **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed`**: the PR body names `skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md` and one eval, but neither the body nor the thread names a card for it. The seat files that card before landing.
- **Dev's out-of-scope note** (restore docblock omits the #28952 seed refusal it does ask): carrier "none". Fold it into the N2 follow-up.
- **SQL push-down**: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The draft lookup is the existing `listDrafts({ type: 'object' })` read, now reached by non-keyed seeds as well; the by-name `readMetaItem` runs only on the path that is about to refuse. No finding.
- **`open_questions`**: the final report carries none.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`18.seed-object-unknown-refused.ts`** — holds against the code and the card.
- Shape matches its sibling `18.picklist-binding-unknown-refused.ts`: `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`, no `conversionIds`, which is right since no mechanical rewrite exists.
- `surface` names the save door in draft and publish mode and the unknown test the code applies (no package registers it, no stored or code-defined object carries it).
- `replacement` states both arms as the code has them: a draft object is enough for a draft seed (the `listDrafts` deferral), a live seed needs the object published (pinned by the "only a draft" publish-save test).
- `reason` is true sentence by sentence: the old 200, the `published` outcome with an empty load, the "publish again" remedy, the 422 at `object`, and the unchanged promotion and restore doors.
- `acceptanceCriteria` is a positive check a consumer can run, on the routes and the `seedApplied.success` field the card itself uses.
- Against the spec on `main`: `SeedSchema.object` is "the machine name of the object to populate". The refusal makes that meaning real at the door and takes no declared capability away.

**`protocol-save-door-refusals.ts`, `protocol-save.ts`, `protocol.ts`** — agree with the contract.
- Only `saveMetaItem` passes `'save'`, and only outside `migrate-stored`. The other two callers (`protocol-history-and-publish.ts`, `protocol-authoring-gate.ts`) pass nothing and are unchanged.
- The unknown test follows the #28990 grant refusal: a registry without `getObject` refuses nothing; `readMetaItem` finding the object means known; a two-holder name refusal means known; any other read error propagates.
- The reorder is safe: a resolved object reaches the same keyed-mode filter and the same `externalId` judgment as before.
- Refusal text: names the seed and the object, says what was looked for (wording differs for a draft and a live save), says why it matters ("publishing it would load no record") and gives both fixes. It is correct in both modes.
- Tried to break it with: a dependency package's object, a legacy prefixed name, a system object, an object only drafted, a seed stored before the rule, and a re-save of such a seed. The first four resolve; the stored seed still publishes; the re-save is refused, which is the intended fix path.

**`build-probes.ts`, `build-probes.user-text.ts`** — agree with the contract.
- `missing` is said only on positive knowledge: the read threw, the engine answers `getSchema` and answers none for the name, and no published object reads. An engine without `getSchema`, or one whose `getSchema` throws, stays `unreadable`.
- `message` and `fix` name the object and tell the author to correct the name or create and publish the object. The person's sentence drops "publish again" as the lone remedy and says the same in all 11 locales. It names the object by API name, which the catalog table now states.
- The card's expected remedy ("names the unknown object") is met.

Nits:
- N1 (nit) — the probe's `readItem` returns `undefined` for a name two packages hold, so that case reads as `missing` when the engine also registers no such object. The save door treats the same refusal as "known". The window is narrow and the effect is wording only. Follow-up or accepted deviation.
- N2 (nit) — `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses` in `protocol.ts` lists what the restore door asks and what it does not, each with its reason. The save door now refuses something the restore door does not ask, and that list does not say so; the reason lives in `unknownSeedObjectRefusal`'s docblock instead, and `protocol.ts` is at its line ceiling. Follow-up card: record it there, together with the #28952 omission, and decide whether a restore should refuse a seed version whose object is gone, as it does for grants.
- N3 (nit) — in ②.

Reviewed-by: `isolated-l2-35388`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3025ade8eb1310b51a3aec79d03d824b56f944e4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.seed-object-unknown-refused.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.user-text.ts

Delta record for PR #35388, card #34864: a merge-only delta on top of the head the first record covers, `468886742c089180014c6d8dc1da1d0c68b59405`. Read: the merge commit and its two parents, the net diff of this head against `main`, what `main` changed between the two bases, os-dev-report 7005072503 on the card, and the 69 check-runs on this head (58 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure).

### ① Derived judgments

- **The head is a merge of the base alone — right.** `3025ade8e` has two parents: the reviewed head `468886742`, and `0967cbe6a`, which is on `main`. It brings in 15 commits of `main` and nothing else.
- **The PR's net diff is unchanged — right.** The diff of this head against its `main` parent is the same 12 files, +387/−48, and its content is identical line for line to the diff the first record judged. `main` touched none of the 12 files between the two bases, so the merge resolved nothing by hand in them.
- **Every judgment of the first record's ① stands as written**: the accept set is narrowed by one value, nothing is widened, the public surface is unchanged, the publish promotion, the restore door and the `migrate-stored` re-save are left as they were, and the spec change is data only.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, and the single marker `registered seed-object-unknown-refused` are all as judged. `main` at this base holds no entry of that id, so the entry is still new here. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` are green on this head.
- N3 (nit) stays an accepted deviation.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dogfood battery — cleared, and pinned to this head.** The newest `os-dev-report` on the card (7005072503, by the relay's identity, naming this pull) opens `dogfood_battery` with `3025ade8e`, which is this head: full battery, no shard and no path filter, exit 0, Test Files 482 passed and 3 skipped, Tests 4092 passed and 68 skipped, no failures. The `--land` gate reads a sha that is the head itself, with no walk needed. `main` changed `label-write.mjs` in this window, but not the dogfood gate or its sha reader.
- **Code `main` moved that the scope reads — checked, no effect.**
  - `readMetaItem` (#34682): a read naming no bundle member now addresses the canonical member alone. That applies only to a type that has bundle members, and `email_template` is the only one; an `object` has none, so the by-name object read the new refusal makes answers as it did.
  - `seed-loader.ts` (#34856): a change to the key a landed row is recorded under. It does not touch how the load reports an object it cannot find, which is the sentence the ledger entry and the changeset rely on.
  - Two new semantic ledger entries arrived from `main`; neither shares this entry's id or surface.
- **Follow-ups**: report 7005072503 names card #35413 as the carrier for N1, N2 and the #28952 docblock note. The `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` card is still not named on the PR body or the thread; the seat files it before landing.
- **SQL push-down**: nothing new; the merge adds no read on the scoped paths.
- **`open_questions`**: none.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

The first record raised none to close. The six scoped files are byte-for-byte what it judged, and the code they read on `main` moved in no way that changes a sentence of the entry, the refusal or the probe. Its ④ stands on this head.

Nits carried, none new: N1 and N2 go to follow-up card #35413; N3 is an accepted deviation.
